subtype: Approach: playing a game with friends instead of alone [Thinking]
passage: Mei noticed that the pull was strongest when she was alone: with nobody around, one round became three hours and the afternoon vanished. So she made a plan. On Saturdays her cousins Freya and Noah came to her flat in Auckland, and that was when the console came out, all three of them shouting at the screen. On other days it stayed in its box. On Wednesday Mei missed it and stared at the box for a while. Then she took her bike out instead. By Saturday the game felt better than ever: Freya laughed so hard at Mei's crash that she fell off the sofa. When the cousins left, playing simply stopped.

qa.q: On which day did Mei's cousins come over?
qa.a: Mei's cousins came over on Saturdays.

qa.q: How did Mei feel on Wednesday when she stared at the box?
qa.a: She felt a pang of missing the game as she stared at the box, but she chose to go cycling instead.

qa.q: What could Mei do if the cousins cannot visit for a few weeks?
qa.a: Play with a friend on a video call for a set time or plan another shared activity, because company is what keeps the game limited and fun.

qa.q: How might Freya see the Saturday game sessions?
qa.a: As great fun, since Freya laughed so hard at Mei's crash that she fell off the sofa.

grounding: A girl finds solo play hard to stop, so she plays only when her cousins are around, which limits time and adds fun.

subtype: Approach: playing a game with friends instead of alone [Thinking]
passage: In the common room of the girls' hostel, the old game console was free most evenings, and Zainab had started slipping down alone after dinner. One level turned into ten. On Wednesday she looked at the clock and realised she had played for two hours by herself and still hadn't written her letter home. Sitting on the stairs, she thought about it. "When I play alone, there's nobody to say stop. When my cousins play, we laugh more, and it ends when the warden calls lights-out." Her cousins, Amandeep and Rubina, lived a floor above. So she made a rule: games only on evenings they came down. That first Saturday the three of them played until the warden's bell, shouting at the screen, and it felt like twice the fun in half the time.

qa.q: How long had Zainab played alone on Wednesday?
What was Zainab thinking on the stairs?
qa.a: Uneasy about the lost time, she realised that playing alone had no natural stopping point.

qa.q: What else could Zainab do on evenings her cousins are busy?
qa.a: Write her letters or read, keeping the console for the shared evenings.

qa.q: How might Amandeep and Rubina experience the new rule?
qa.a: They get a cousin to play with and livelier evenings together.

grounding: A hostel girl who feels the pull of playing alone decides to game only with her cousins, which limits time and adds fun.

subtype: Approach: playing a game with friends instead of alone [Thinking]
passage: I'm Preeti, Devika's older cousin, and I live in the same building. Last term, whenever I came up, Devika was alone in her room with the tablet and earphones, hardly looking up while her mother called her name. Then one day Devika told me, "I'm only going to play when you and Rinku are here." I thought she was joking. But now, when Rinku and I come up on Sunday afternoons, she pulls out the tablet and we play the island game together, all three crowded on the bed, arguing about which bridge to build. When we leave, she puts the tablet back on the shelf. On weekdays I see her reading on the balcony instead. I don't know what made her decide, but she seems happier.

qa.q: When do Preeti and Rinku come up?
Why might Devika have decided to play only with her cousins?
qa.a: Playing alone may have felt lonely and hard to stop, while playing together is more fun and ends naturally.

qa.q: What else could Devika do if her cousins stop visiting for a while?
qa.a: Agree a short weekend time with her mother, so the game stays limited without them.

qa.q: How does Preeti see the change?
qa.a: Preeti thinks Devika seems happier, though Preeti isn't sure what made Devika decide.

grounding: A cousin notices a girl now plays only when her cousins visit, which limits her gaming and makes it more fun.
